title: Whole accusation narrative with causal rebuttal, temporal rebuttal and non-entailing outcome
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED. The complete wolf-and-lamb fable separates two disproved allegations from the narrator’s commitments, a new father referent and a final violent outcome that does not validate either charge.

design.structural_baseline: Directed composition, hierarchy at spaces, whole-form residuals and entry effects are retained structural facts, not meanings. No confirmed lexical anchor is required to explore a declared whole hypothesis.
design.writer_status: UNBOUND. No target alphabet, fixed header/count, one-clause-per-group, per-occurrence gloss, hidden filler or retrospective quoted-scope repair is proposed.
design.access: No raw target packet, image, reserve or GDT990 model/runtime/result opened. Bounded legacy navigation unexpectedly displayed already-public target lines in ROUND4_CONTENT_DECISION.md; no use was made of those strings. Consequently this entire supply run is not claimed target-character-blind.
design.review_limit: Bounded route/topic/search plus IDEA31/33 primary review and closest source proposals. Not exhaustive novelty review or experimental selection.

whole_content_inventory.content: The wolf and lamb reach the same stream because of thirst; wolf stands above, lamb far below. Same stream is not a claim that one indivisible water portion is reused.
Narrator calls the wolf a robber and gives fauce improba as the motive for starting a quarrel. Ravenous/malicious appetite is an interpretation; the expression is preserved in the Latin.
Wolf alleges the lamb has muddied the water for him while he drinks. The question carries an accusation, not an authorial assertion that muddying occurred.
The fearful wool-bearer, identified as the lamb by continuity, asks how that is possible: water flows from the wolf to the lamb’s drinking place. The flow objection concerns causal direction.
Narrator says the wolf was repulsed by the force of truth; this licenses endorsement of the rebuttal within the story.
Wolf alleges a verbal offense against himself six months earlier.
Lamb answers that it had not yet been born; temporal existence is the second, independent prerequisite for the alleged action.

Wolf substitutes the lamb’s father as alleged offender. Father is a new participant related to the lamb, not a pronoun or synonym for the lamb. No reply establishes whether the father actually offended.
Wolf seizes and tears the lamb in an unjust killing. A completed violent outcome does not turn the earlier charges into facts.
The narrator explicitly says the fable is written against people who oppress the innocent with invented causes. The general moral and authorial purpose belong to the complete content.

design.hypothesis: A whole passage may preserve an argument whose local factual corrections change warranted commitments, although the acting participant refuses those corrections. The complete narrative and moral, not only quoted allegations, are part of the provisional content.
design.composition_policy: Speech changes first/second-person reference by one global speaker/addressee rule. Narrator assertions, reported accusations and rebuttal contents have fixed different commitment types. Father is explicitly introduced once and is not allowed to replace the lamb elsewhere. These are a finite conceptual policy, not a selected target serializer.
design.coupled_consequence: Upstream/downstream identity governs whether the first allegation is physically warranted, and birth relative to the earlier date governs the second. Refutation preserves the same alleged recipient and accused participant until the father substitution. The final act is compatible with rejected accusations because action and truth commitment are distinct.

rivals.rule: Every embedded proposition is asserted true by the narrator.
rivals.contrast: The two charges conflict with the explicitly endorsed flow rebuttal and the birth-time rebuttal.

rivals.rule: Successful rebuttal necessarily blocks the next action.
rivals.contrast: The source proceeds to unjust killing.

rivals.rule: A realized punitive outcome certifies the charge as true.
rivals.contrast: The narrator explicitly frames invented causes and innocence.

rivals.rule: Father is another expression for the lamb.
rivals.contrast: The third charge would collapse to the already rebutted age-dependent second one and erase the source’s new relationship.

costs_and_symmetries: Consistent relabeling of wolf/lamb names remains possible unless independently bounded; causal roles alone do not identify animal species.
The father accusation remains unverified, not an established event or an independently disproved fact.
Narrator-to-character aliases robber/wolf and wool-bearer/lamb are interpretation obligations, not free extra target meanings.
Flow reasoning is the source’s endorsed argument; no modern fluid experiment is claimed.
A generic correctly scoped reported-speech account already fits; the source does not identify a unique evidential word or a writing code.

predecessors.retained: A report association can reflect topic/genre; no no-interaction null or target evidential marker is inferred.
Contrast itself does not identify the connector.

Proposed versus accepted opinion already exists in net-contribution content and has no target writer. This proposal’s additional consequence is two different factual prerequisites followed by action contrary to warranted judgment, not another payment calculation.
Transport safety and cargo identity are different constraints. Shared animal/water vocabulary does not reopen that route.

design.smallest_future_decision: A later joint whole reading must commit to all speaker scopes and participant references before checking both rebuttals and the final moral/action relation. It cannot label individual contradictions as quoted material after the fact. No target is selected now.
design.likely_failure: Fable genre has no nominated target or admitted illustration owner; lexical and speech-boundary freedom may erase the discriminator. Historical plausibility of the work does not establish manuscript source identity.

source_evidence.quote: ## B. A rebuttal changes what is warranted, not necessarily what happens

source.work: Phaedrus, Fabulae I.1, Lupus et Agnus, complete15-line fable
source.historical_date: Roman imperial Latin work conventionally attributed to first-centuryCE Phaedrus; no medieval manuscript was collated in this task.
source.witness: IntraText Latin digital text. Its exact printed-edition ancestry is not established here. A Perseus1876Mueller search record was only a navigation comparator; its text endpoint and attempted XML fetch failed and are not claimed as the owned edition.
source.normalization: HTML text only, whitespace collapsed, one final newline; complete from Ad rivum eundem through qui fictis causis innocentes opprimunt. Fifteen verse lines retained as conventional locators in the inventory, not target boundaries.
source_ambiguities: The father accusation is reported but not separately verified or refuted.
Water/liquor names a flowing medium; no conservation or whole-portion identity is asserted.
The spatial impossibility is the story’s endorsed causal reasoning, not a new hydraulic experiment.
Narrator, wolf, lamb and father are distinct discourse roles; moral oppressors and innocents generalize the story rather than introducing extra on-scene animals.
Verse form, capitalization and punctuation do not license a Voynich writer or a fixed group count.
